title: Microscopy Analysis of Wear Mechanisms of Reinforced Composites Materials
content: Leading edge erosion is an emerging problem in wind turbine blade reliability, causing performance decline and additional maintenance costs. The topic of erosion in composite materials has received substantial attention in the last decades, the interest in this area is proportional to the increasing use of composite materials in the aerospace industry, where they can be subjected to multiple impacts of solid or liquid particles, where durability is a primary consideration [1,2]. Wind turbine blades are mainly made of fiberglass, but recent studies have shown that this material has lower resistance to erosive wear, therefore the use of carbon fiber in the leading edge of wind turbine blades is proposed, which will reduce this phenomenon caused by the impact of solid and liquid particles, and in turn avoid losses in the efficiency of electric power generation [3]. Sareen, Sapre and Michael (2013) investigated the effect of blade leading edge erosion on wind turbine performance. They obtained results that revealed that leading edge erosion can be significantly detrimental to airfoil performance. Erosion also caused a substantial reduction in the lift coefficient, especially at the higher angles of attack that wind turbines experience during operation [4]. Vite et al. (2013) mention that erosion wear on a solid surface is generated due to the impact of hard solid particles. This type of wear is common in industrial and manufacturing processes [5]. Castorrini (2016) in his study on the computational analysis of rain erosion on wind turbine blades, demonstrates that the damage caused by rain erosion on blades can be significant if the blades are not protected. This damage would not typically influence the structural integrity of the blades, but could degrade the aerodynamic performance and therefore the power output [6]. Carbon fibers are recommended as a promising solution for the manufacture of wind turbine blades since they have greater rigidity and better mechanical properties [7].
